questions.q: How much can profits grow by keeping a small share of customers loyal?
a: As much as 85 percent
As much as 15 percent
As much as 40 percent
As much as 60 percent
questions.why: Lesson 1 says retaining even a small percentage of customers can lift profits by up to 85 percent.

questions.q: What does the H in H.O.U.R.S. stand for?
a: Be human and tailor your response
Hire more support staff
Hide the complaint from the public
Hold a meeting about the issue
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the first step is to treat complainers as people and personalize your reply.

questions.q: What does using one channel mean?
a: Fix the issue without forwarding the customer
Reply on every platform at once
Move the complaint to a FAQ page
Ask the customer to call back later
questions.why: Lesson 2 says not to pass customers around or send them elsewhere, just solve the problem.

questions.q: What does the F in F.E.A.R. stand for?
a: Find public complaints online
Fix the problem privately
Follow up after a week
Forward it to a manager
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to use tools like Google Alerts to locate public complaints.

questions.q: What should you do after replying once in public?
a: Keep it short, then switch channels for privacy
Reply repeatedly until the customer stops
Delete the thread to protect the brand
Ask other customers to defend you
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends one reply and moving to email when the issue is personal.
